scope: Jetson Orin Nano as a test hub without the arms: offline suites, control center through an SSH tunnel, YOLO26n detect + pose on CPU, CUDA PyTorch and TensorRT, a live C270 loop, and temperatures. No arm, no CAN/USB adapter, no pickup_server, no Dream key, nothing posted.
where: ~/hub-tests on the Jetson only (fresh clone and isolated venvs). ~/geotech-robotics-hackathon, ~/jetson-runtime (its Python was only run for the arm tests) and ~/jetson-prep-assets were not touched. No sudo, no system settings changed.

cuda_pytorch.finding: The plain PyPI torch 2.15.0 for aarch64 is a CUDA 13.2 build and works on the Orin under JetPack 7.2.1: torch.cuda.is_available() True, device 'Orin' (8, 7), a GPU matmul ran. Its arch list is sm_80..sm_120 without sm_87; sm_80 code runs on sm_87. No NVIDIA Jetson-specific wheel index was needed. vision/README.md says plain pip gives a CPU-only build; that was true for JetPack 6, not here.

still_images.method: Same as the Mac check: imgsz 640, conf 0.25, adapter_ms is one UltralyticsDetector call (detect + pose + conversion), median of 10 after one warm-up; inference_ms is Ultralytics' own per-model time.
still_images.repeatability: A second .pt run from the script (commit 9ceef72) gave CPU 357-379 ms and CUDA 69-78 ms, same labels.

labels.pt_cpu_and_cuda: Identical to the Mac on all 5 stills (side cylinder: bottle 0.33 + hand 0.856 -> HAND empty_hand; wrist cylinder: cup 0.517 -> EMPTY; woman_hands: 2 hands -> HAND multiple_hands; bus: 9 person, 8 hand; synthetic can: cup 0.84).
labels.engines_fp32_and_fp16: Differ from .pt on 3 of 5 stills: side cylinder loses the 0.33 bottle and gains a second hand (HAND multiple_hands instead of empty_hand); wrist cylinder cup 0.517 -> 0.753 and 2 persons; bus 8 person, 7 hand. FP16 matches FP32 within 0.003. Likely cause: the engines are fixed 640x640 (padded) while .pt predicts on a rectangular letterbox. Tune and test thresholds on the engines you will run.

tensorrt.system_trtexec: not installed (/usr/src/tensorrt absent, no trtexec on PATH, no libnvinfer packages); not installed with apt because that needs sudo
tensorrt.trt11_fp16: yolo export format=engine quantize=16 with tensorrt-cu13 11.4.0.106 FAILED after the ONNX step: 'No module named modelopt'. Ultralytics 8.4.207 needs nvidia-modelopt[onnx] for FP16 on TensorRT 11 (strongly typed only) and itself asks for tensorrt-cu13 >=10.15,<11. modelopt was not installed (it would also change nvidia-cusparselt in that venv).
tensorrt.trt11_fp32: yolo export format=engine device=0 (no quantize) worked: yolo26n.engine 159.1 MB in 136 s, yolo26n-pose.engine 82.2 MB in 153 s
tensorrt.trt10_fp16: In venv-trt10 (tensorrt-cu13 10.16.1.11 from PyPI; its sdist pulls the wheel from NVIDIA's pip index), yolo export format=engine quantize=16 device=0 worked: yolo26n.engine 8.1 MB in 512 s, yolo26n-pose.engine 9.5 MB in about 11 min. sha256 df137906236396cbf5eb133b339d5406db65e4b8ba8590f47416ed5b00104445 and f24ff05bf0492f549998cb8cb19be383bfa1c4443647a757eadab94a070d1ede (board-specific, not portable, git-ignored, kept in ~/hub-tests/engines-fp16)

live_c270.camera: Logitech C270 /dev/video0 (index 0), V4L2, 640x480 YUYV. fuser showed it free before each run. The room was dark (mean pixel 44/255), so the C270 ran at 15 fps (raw read 68 ms per frame), not 30. Nobody was in front of it at 4 AM: no hand or can moments were exercised.

runs.path: TensorRT FP16 engines (TRT 10.16, from the script)

live_c270.reading: frame_latency_ms is read start to decision. When the detector is faster than the camera (engines) it equals the camera's frame period (about 67 ms at 15 fps), so the engines are camera-bound here; when slower (CUDA .pt, about 75 ms) frames queue in the V4L2 buffer and get stale. max is the first frame: model load and CUDA/TensorRT warm-up (5 s, 12 s for the FP16 venv). Warm up before trusting the first seconds.
live_c270.telemetry: Sessions jetson-c270-live-cpu-20261108 (18 events), jetson-c270-live-gpu-20261108 (27), jetson-c270-live-trt-fp32-20261108 (28) and jetson-c270-trt-fp16-20261108-042701 (21) under ~/hub-tests/sessions; all four validate with 0 invalid; the first two were also served through the tunnel API.
live_c270.unexplained: The CPU path is 2.3x slower per frame inside vision.run (877 ms on the stills clip too, so not the camera) than in still_check (375 ms) with the same adapter; tegrastats showed 1-2 busy cores in the loop vs all 6 in still_check; torch reports 6 threads either way. Not investigated further; CPU at about 1 fps is not a demo option anyway.

thermals.reading: The fan is spinning and responds (58 -> 66 PWM). Junction stayed at or below 52.5 C over about 45 minutes of mixed load, far below throttling. Runs were 30 s to 10 min; a sustained hour at the demo, in a warmer room or in an enclosure, is not covered.

verdict: The Orin Nano is a usable test hub tonight without the arms: every offline suite runs (failures above are a host-dependent test and a filename-case bug, both reproducible), the control center serves through the tunnel, and YOLO26n + pose run on the GPU from plain PyPI wheels. Best path: TensorRT FP16 engines at about 35 ms per frame for both models (5-6 ms inference each), camera-bound at 15 fps in a dark room. CUDA .pt is about 75 ms; CPU is not usable (about 375 ms, 1 fps in the loop).
not_established: Hands, a held can or any handoff moment on the C270 (nobody in view; dark room).
Sustained thermals over a full demo, and power independence of the kit.
The --show preview on the KVM display (all runs were headless).
Any arm, CAN, pickup_server or Dream round trip from the Jetson.
Whether the engine-vs-.pt label differences hold on real camera frames.
